question: Do label-trained token weights add information beyond a frozen sentence embedding for comparing two texts?
representations: Use the same pinned GTE Transformer for both probes. Cache each training text's last-layer token vectors without labels. On each fitting partition separately estimate feature scales and train a shared preference head by pairwise binary cross entropy. The first head uses mean token pooling. The second can additionally weight a token using the common context of both alternatives. Swapping the alternatives must reverse the logit. Both heads get the same training-only scaled style differences.
training: Seed 11419, three epochs, AdamW, batch size 96, learning rate 0.001, weight decay 0.04, dropout 0.12. Each complete training trajectory is one supervised fit. No early stopping on the evaluation partition. Explicit fit receipts precede each optimization.
screen: Compare each single and its equal probability blend with the preceding linear GTE production candidate on the same primary fold. Lock the best positive alternative, breaking ties in favor of the simpler option. Confirm exactly this choice on the other two group-disjoint evaluation folds; stop if confirmation_1 has no positive gain. Promotion requires a positive gain on all three and pooled gain at least 0.003. At most four new fits and zero model API calls. This is research and cannot establish a new production score by itself.
held_data: Only the archived training payloads are opened. No designated validation inputs or labels and no official test or H2. These raw encoders are general-purpose frozen features; the head is trained on each fold's permitted labels.
